cues.en: All right.
In this section we are going to learn about backtracking.
Backtracking is a problem solving technique that systematically explore all possible solutions to a
problem.
So if a choice leads to the invalid solution, it backtracks to the previous step and tries to a different
path.
So you can think of this as trying all possibilities step by step and doing choices when they don't
work, and saving time by skipping the invalid options early.
So the simple real life example for backtracking can be choosing an outfit.
So let's say you are picking an outfit from the following items.
You have three shirts in color of red, blue and white, and you have two pants in color of black and
blue.
And you have two shoes, sneakers and boots, which is white and black.
Now you want to find all possible stylish combinations, so backtracking will work like this.
First, let's say you are selecting the red shirt.
Then we are going to pair it with the next pant.
So the pant is going to be blue.
So let's say in this case you don't like this.
So you are going to eliminate this option.
So you will go to back and select the next pant.
So the next pant is black.
So we see that they pair with each other.
So we can continue to select the boot.
So in this case this is going to be our one option.
Now if you are looking for all possible options we are going to continue back and select the next shirt.
Now the next t shirt is blue.
So we are going to pair it with blue.
So let's say we don't like it.
So we are going to continue back and select the next pant.
So the next pant is going to be black pant.
So let's say these are pair.
So we are going to continue to select the shoes.
So let's say in this case we are going to select the white shoes.
So let's say they are not pair.
So we are going to go back and select the next row.
So the next row is going to be the boot which is black.
So that's how the backtracking works in case of the selecting outfit.
So as you can see every time we are selecting the an option.
So if this is not the solution we are going to go back and select it in different options so we can
explain the backtracking using the tree.
So backtracking can be visualized as exploring a tree of the possibilities.
So in the root we will have the initial state.
So let's say we have the each level which represents t shirts pants and shoes.
So let's say in the first level we have the t shirt.
So in this case we're just going to put it like this.
So here we have three t shirts which are red blue and white.
Then we are going to pair them with the each pant.
So we saw that we have the two pants which are black and blue.
So that's why we are going to pair each t shirt with the with any of them.
Then we have the shoes which are sneakers and boots white and black.
So we are going to pair them with these pants also.
So that's how we can visualize the all options in the tree and select the ones which are the solutions
for our problem.
So here the step for backtracking is that we are choosing an option and checking that if this is valid,
we are going to continue to explore the next branch.
If this is not valid, we are going to continue until the solutions will fail.
So let's say if we start with red t shirt, we are going to continue to do black pant.
So if this is not working we will come back and continue to do blue pant.
So if this is not working we are going to continue to the next t shirt.
So here we are exploring the all options until we find the solution.
So as we mentioned the steps over here can be like this.
Choose an option.
Then check if this is meeting the constraint.
Then repeat until all solutions fine.
Now the key features of backtracking is that we are choosing an option and testing all possibilities
for each option, and undo changes if they lead to invalid option, and skip the entire set of the invalid
options using the constraint.
Now there are many problems that can be solved using backtracking.
We can use backtracking for word search puzzles.
We can solve the maze, explore the paths, and backtrack on the dead ends.
And one of the famous problem which can be solved with backtracking is N-queens problem.
So we are going to look this one in the next lecture.
